title: Zero-friction SDK boarding checklist and UX scribbles
content:
Context:
Small working document to capture a minimal, high-confidence path for new engineers and integrators to get an SDK-powered LLM call running against Redwood in <= 10 minutes. Focus: remove friction points that cause drop-off during first-run (auth, env, errors, observability). This is intentionally pragmatic and opinionated — trade polish for clarity and measurable success metrics.

Problem statement (observed):
- New users get blocked by: API key placement, firewall/network hints, missing example models, confusing error messages, and lack of visible telemetry.
- Engineers bounce between README -> example app -> local env issues and rarely reach a successful instrumented call.
- Our current Quickstart has too many choices (models, endpoints, SDK modes) and not enough guardrails.

Goals (measurable):
- 70% of new signups run a successful tokenized call in < 10 minutes (measured by onboarding event).
- 50% of those enable basic telemetry (sdk.initialized + sdk.call.completed).
- Reduce first-hour support tickets about "401 / permission" and "network timeout" by 40%.

Principles for zero-friction flow:
- Opinionated defaults: pick one model and one route for the 0–10 minute path. Avoid branching.
- Fail fast, explain clearly: predictable error codes + friendly remediation text.
- Local-first reproducibility: small script that runs without cloud infra (mock or client-side playground) then swaps in real key.
- Telemetry by default: opt-out (not opt-in) for basic onboarding events (with clear privacy copy).
- One-file starter: single script (or single well-documented command) that demonstrates the whole loop.

Proposed Quickstart flow (10-minute path):
1) Create account & copy API key (existing flow)
2) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter-lite
3) open quickstart/onefile.js (or .py) and paste API_KEY into top comment or export REDWOOD_API_KEY
4) run: npm run quickstart (or python quickstart.py) — script does: install deps, run a small prompt, prints tokens, example output, and uploads a minimal trace to dev console (if key flagged as dev)
5) Success screen: printed tokens, latency, model used, link to Console trace with pre-filtered trace id.

onefile.js (sketch):
- Header: short privacy blurb: "SDK will emit minimal onboarding events: sdk.initialized, sdk.call.start, sdk.call.end. No input text sent to analytics unless you opt-in to sharing examples."
- config: const SDK = require('@redwood/sdk'); const client = new SDK({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || '<PASTE_HERE>' });
- small prompt + streaming demo + error handling with remediation.

CLI quickstart command examples (for local dev and CI):
- redwood sdk init --auth=env --yes   # write minimal config to ~/.redwoodrc
- redwood sdk quickstart --model=redwood-alpha-1 --once
- redwood sdk telemetry opt-out --off  # explicit explain how to opt-out

Minimal config file (~/.redwoodrc) example:
- {
-   "default_model": "redwood-alpha-1",
-   "region": "us-west-2",
-   "telemetry": "on",
-   "timeout_ms": 12000
- }

Telemetry + observability (required for success metrics):
- Onboarding events to emit (names and minimal schema):
-   sdk.initialized -> { method: "onefile", env: "local", sdk_version }
-   sdk.call.start -> { model, input_len, request_id }
-   sdk.call.end -> { request_id, tokens_consumed, latency_ms, status }
- Privacy: events should never include prompt text unless user explicitly enables "share-sample-prompt: true" in ~/.redwoodrc.
- Console UX: quickstart should open a pre-filtered Console view with the request_id in the URL so users see live traces and token breakdown.

Error taxonomy + friendly remediation text (examples):
- 401 Unauthorized: "Can't access your key. Did you paste the API key or set REDWOOD_API_KEY? Try: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx"
- Network timeout: "Check your firewall / proxy. Try again with --region=us-west-2 or run with --offline-mock to verify client works without network."
- Rate limited (429): "You're on the free tier. We applied a soft limit. Upgrade or wait 60s. See quota helper: redwood account quota"
- Model mismatch: "The quickstart uses redwood-alpha-1. If you can't access it, run: redwood sdk quickstart --model=small-open-1"

Onboarding instrumentation: gating events and where to store them
- Emit onboarding events to our ingestion pipeline with sample rate 1. Backfill logic for replay if user later consents.
- Add a lightweight SDK shim that batches telemetry to reduce noisy network calls.

Small UX experiments to run (A/B):
- A: current multi-choice quickstart (control)
- B: single-opinionated quickstart + preopened Console link (treatment)
- Metrics: time-to-first-successful-call, percent enabling telemetry, NPS-like micro-survey after first success.

Developer docs outline (short):
- Quickstart (onefile): copy-paste run -> success screen -> Console link
- Local dev troubleshooting: common failures + commands
- Telemetry & privacy: what we collect and how to opt-out
- Next steps: sample app (embedder chat UI) + production checklist

Acceptance criteria for this initiative:
- One-file quickstart that runs in < 10 minutes on Mac/Linux/Windows WSL without extra config (CI smoke test added).
- SDK emits the three onboarding events and Console shows the trace link from the quickstart run.
- README success rate measured in GA or internal analytics, target above.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy/legal: need sign-off for opt-out-by-default telemetry. Loop in security/compliance (RED-2310).
- Which model should be the opinionated default? redwood-alpha-1 or a smaller public model to avoid quota/limits for new accounts? (tradeoff: fidelity vs availability)
- Should the quickstart require a network call (real) or be able to run fully offline first with a mocked server to build confidence?

Next steps (short, actionable):
- (Owner: Priya) Draft the onefile quickstart in JS + Py prototypes, add to repo: sdk-starter-lite (due 2025-03-07).
- (Owner: Alex) Add onboarding events schema to telemetry team, get fast-path ingestion (due 2025-03-10).
- (Owner: Samir) Create PR for CLI flags and config write logic (POC branch: cli/quickstart) (due 2025-03-12).
- Schedule 30m design review with Security and Docs (calendar: #sdk-onboard-review).

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep language minimal: "Get started in 3 commands" > long paragraphs.
- Consider a tiny web-based runner that runs in browser using wasm for local demo. Might be a future micro experiment after core CLI flow is stable.
- If privacy sign-off slow, ship skeleton with telemetry off-by-default but with an in-console prompt to enable sharing for product improvements.

References and links:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482  (starter script sketch)
- Jira: RED-1234 (onboarding metric tracking), RED-2310 (telemetry privacy review)
- Confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/SDK+Onboarding+Hypotheses

Quick checklist (for PR reviewers):
- [ ] onefile quickstart present for JS and Py
- [ ] CLI: redwood sdk quickstart command + --yes flag
- [ ] emits sdk.initialized / sdk.call.start / sdk.call.end events
- [ ] friendly error messages for top 4 errors
- [ ] README: 3-command flow + Console link behavior documented
- [ ] Security sign-off on telemetry or opt-out plan attached

End of notes.
